clue.text: Maori woman, with a head for hock, tucking into something like hock

indicators.note: the pair of pieces is tucked inside the wine, sitting within it

parts.note: hock is a German white wine, so something like it is wine

indicators.note: the head of the word hock is its first letter

explanation.surface: A Maori woman, slightly tipsy, is seen with a glass of hock and something like it.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'hock' is the source of the head letter; the first is defined loosely as a wine. A and H go inside WINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Wahine is the Maori (and Hawaiian) word for a woman or wife, used in New Zealand English.

clue.text: Features of boat or features of canal engrossing one

indicators.note: to engross is to absorb or take in, so the little word holds the single letter

parts.note: taken as written
one as an indefinite article gives A
a canal has locks to raise and lower boats

explanation.surface: A comparison of what you see on a boat with what you see on a canal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' looks like a mere link but supplies two letters, which absorb A (one); canal locks follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Rowlocks, called oarlocks in American usage, are the fittings on a boat's gunwale that hold the oars.

clue.text: Produce new design for border of speed-limit sign?

parts.note: a UK speed-limit sign is a white disc edged with a red ring, a red O
a UK speed-limit sign is a white disc edged with a red ring, a red O

explanation.surface: A designer is asked to rework the edging on a road sign.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain speed limits are shown as numbers inside a red circle, so the border is a RED O.
explanation.definitionFit: To redo something is to do it over again, as when a design is reworked from scratch.

clue.text: Continue silent, holding in to the absolute deadline

parts.note: to last is to continue or go on

indicators.note: the word for silent holds the little word inside it

parts.note: mute means silent

explanation.surface: Someone is told to keep quiet and stay in right up to the final moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link word but supplies its own two letters, which 'holding' puts inside the word for silent.
explanation.definitionFit: The last minute is the latest possible moment before something is due, a final cut-off.

clue.text: Understand French is represented in collated material

parts.note: dig is slang for understand, as in 'do you dig it?'
est is French for 'is'

explanation.surface: A student grasps how French grammar appears in a compilation.
explanation.definitionFit: A digest is a compilation or summary of material gathered from various sources.

clue.text: A little boy seizing an insect

indicators.note: the word for boy grabs and holds the insect inside it

parts.note: a son is a boy
a midge is a small flying insect

explanation.surface: A small boy grabs hold of a bug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A little' looks like it describes the boy, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A smidgeon, also spelt smidgen, is a very small amount, a tiny bit.

clue.text: Each label's attached to last of usable fodder

parts.note: a tag is a label

indicators.note: the last of the word usable is its final letter

explanation.surface: Every tag is fixed to the final bit of fodder that can be used.
explanation.definitionFit: Eatage is grazing or grass available for animals to eat, a dialect term for pasture fodder.

clue.text: Is male in vintage car displaying personality?

indicators.note: the pieces sit inside the old vehicle

parts.note: chara is short for charabanc, an old-fashioned motor coach

explanation.surface: A man shows off his personality in an old car.
explanation.walkthrough: A charabanc, often shortened to chara, was an early open-topped motor coach used for outings in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Charisma is a compelling attractiveness or force of personality that draws others in.

clue.text: Most attractive trial doing for scoundrel finally

indicators.note: doing for something is replacing it, so one word takes another's place
finally points at the final letter of the scoundrel word as the one replaced

parts.note: a cur is a scoundrel, a contemptible man
a test is a trial

explanation.surface: A trial undoes a villain at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doing for' means replacing; 'finally' picks the last letter of CUR, the R, which TEST replaces.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutest is the superlative of cute, meaning most charming or attractive.

clue.text: Military camp bad for positioning in height?

indicators.note: the pieces are placed inside the abbreviation for height

parts.note: ill means bad, as in ill will
taken as written

explanation.surface: A camp site is judged badly placed on high ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'height' looks like a hill but gives only HT, which holds ILL and FOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A hill fort is an ancient fortified camp built on a hilltop, typically of the Iron Age.

clue.text: Inclines to adopt right fashions

indicators.note: the word for inclines takes in the letter, adopting it

parts.note: tends means inclines, as in tends to agree

explanation.surface: Someone leans towards picking up the correct styles.
explanation.definitionFit: Trends are fashions or the current general directions in which styles are moving.

clue.text: Some annoyance recalled about a copper drinking-vessel

indicators.note: the reversed word goes around the pieces that follow
recalled means called back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a pet is a fit of sulking annoyance, as in 'in a pet'
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A slight irritation is remembered about a copper mug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns PET to TEP, which goes about A and CU.
explanation.definitionFit: A teacup is a small cup for drinking tea from, one kind of drinking vessel.

clue.text: Run with comic phrase when performing in part of theatre

indicators.note: performing suggests the letters are put through their paces into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An actor delivers a funny line during a run of a play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comic' looks like the anagram signal but its letters are part of the fodder; 'performing' rearranges RUN plus COMICPHRASE.
explanation.definitionFit: The proscenium arch frames the stage in a traditional theatre, separating stage from auditorium.

clue.text: Flit west, flying bird

indicators.note: flying suggests the letters scatter and land in another order

explanation.surface: A bird flits off westward in flight.
explanation.definitionFit: A swiftlet is a small Asian swift, some species of which build the nests used in bird's-nest soup.

clue.text: US actor, male, not quite Rock

parts.note: he is the male pronoun

indicators.note: not quite means the word falls short by its last letter

parts.note: a stone is a rock

explanation.surface: A male American actor almost has the stature of Rock Hudson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock' looks like a name (Rock Hudson) but is STONE minus its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlton Heston was an American film actor famous for Ben-Hur and The Ten Commandments.

clue.text: Hot at the same level around area — blissful

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

indicators.note: the word for level goes around the abbreviation

parts.note: evenly means at the same level

explanation.surface: A warm, level spread around an area feels delightful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts EVENLY round A after H.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavenly means delightful or wonderful, as blissful as paradise.

clue.text: Acting coach, by inference?

parts.note: a bus is a coach
kin means related; a bus is inferred to be related to a coach

explanation.surface: Drama coaching is offered, apparently by implication.
explanation.walkthrough: The buskin, a high boot worn by Greek tragic actors, stands for tragedy and acting; read as BUS KIN it is a bus's relative, a coach.
explanation.definitionFit: Buskin by metonymy stands for tragic drama or the art of acting, from the boots worn on stage.

clue.text: Significant piece blocked by Knight — it's time for some craft

indicators.note: the chess piece is blocked, filled in the middle, by the other pieces

parts.note: the king is the most important piece in chess
N is the chess notation for knight
taken as written

explanation.surface: A chess game where a knight blocks a key piece and time is called.
explanation.walkthrough: In chess notation the knight is N, since K is already taken by the king; 'it's' splits as 'it' plus a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Knitting is a handicraft of looping yarn with needles, a common domestic craft.

clue.text: Untroubled visit taking in soldiers and navy

indicators.note: the word for visit takes the pieces inside it

parts.note: to see someone is to visit them
RE is the Royal Engineers, British Army soldiers

explanation.surface: A calm visit includes a tour of the army and navy.
explanation.definitionFit: Serene means calm and peaceful, undisturbed by worry.

clue.text: Channel showing most of Quixote's locale (Spain)

indicators.note: most of a word means it loses its last letter

parts.note: Don Quixote was from La Mancha in central Spain
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: A tour channel shows most of Don Quixote's home region in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Channel' looks like a TV station, but it is the sea between England and France.
explanation.definitionFit: La Manche is the French name for the English Channel, meaning 'the sleeve'.

clue.text: On, though acting without much impact

parts.note: a is an abbreviation for acting in dictionaries
light means having little weight or force

explanation.surface: A performance is under way, though the acting barely registers.
explanation.definitionFit: Alight means burning, lit, as in a lamp that is on.

clue.text: Puzzle, one of Phi's recalled, with good content

indicators.note: content means contained, so the letter sits inside the reversed pieces
recalled means called back, so the words are read backwards

parts.note: one as an indefinite article gives A
the setter Phi refers to his own, so Phi's is mine

explanation.surface: The setter Phi remembers one of his own puzzles, with a good filling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one of Phi's' is A MINE, reversed by 'recalled' to ENIMA, with G inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An enigma is a puzzle or mystery, something baffling to work out.

clue.text: Post sent round North America capital

indicators.note: the word for post goes round the single letter

parts.note: mail is post

explanation.surface: Letters are sent around North America and to a capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'North America' is split as N and A: N goes into MAIL, A follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Manila is the capital city of the Philippines.

clue.text: Runs from way of manacling soldiers

indicators.note: runs come away from the iron fetter, removed from it

parts.note: a leg iron is a shackle fastened round the ankle
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Captive soldiers escape their shackles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runs from' looks like fleeing; it means R is removed from LEG IRON.
explanation.definitionFit: A legion is a body of soldiers, originally a Roman army unit.

clue.text: Very difficult, no longer foremost in 15?

indicators.note: foremost means first, so it is placed at the front of the other piece

parts.note: ex means former, no longer what one was
the answer to 15 across is defined as acting

explanation.surface: A former actor found the stage taxing.
explanation.walkthrough: 15 across's definition, 'Acting', supplies the second piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Exacting means demanding great effort or care, hard to satisfy.

clue.text: See 12
A nasty character snatches what in pub?

indicators.note: the word for nasty character snatches and holds the interjection

parts.note: a louse is a contemptible person
eh is an exclamation meaning what?

explanation.surface: A villain grabs something in a bar, and someone asks what.
explanation.definitionFit: An alehouse is a tavern or public house where ale is sold.

clue.text: Prison Director guided to reduce light

parts.note: can is slang for prison

indicators.note: to reduce means to cut short, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: led means guided

explanation.surface: A prison governor is told to cut the lighting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduce light' reads as dimming, but 'light' is the definition and 'to reduce' trims LED.
explanation.definitionFit: A candle is a wax stick with a wick, burnt as a source of light.
